curriculum.title: Trace the hand
curriculum.make: The alphabet blocks traced into outlines: each box found, its ruled lines lifted off, the capital and small letter parted, the pen line followed.
curriculum.ask: What did the tracing keep, and what did it leave on the paper? (The boxes were ruled by the same hand: lifting them off was a choice.)
curriculum.suits: an afternoon of tracing, and someone nearby to wonder why a copy is never quite the thing

curriculum.title: A pen from a hand
curriculum.make: A pen measured from the letters (its line and a stroke's width) draws the digits, marks and the twelve sigils the sheet did not hold. Each says it was penned.
curriculum.ask: Which letters did a person draw, and which did a machine draw in their manner? How can you tell — and should it have to tell you?
curriculum.suits: spotting the difference first, then asking where else it is not said

curriculum.title: Letter blocks
curriculum.make: Write any word in the hand, in boxes like the sheet's, and see it come apart into the sounds it makes.
curriculum.ask: Which letters make one sound together? Say a word slowly with someone who reads it differently, and see where you split it.
curriculum.suits: sounding words out slowly, side by side; anyone learning English letters

curriculum.title: Tune the projection
curriculum.make: A Spw expression sets how the hand is shown: ~ lets it wander, % weighs it, @ leans it, # shows the measure, * shows it as scanned. The tuning travels in the address (?/texture.website/@spwashi/=~2), so a tuned picture can be passed along and read before it is opened.
curriculum.ask: When a picture is changed on purpose, what should it say about that? Read an address aloud: can you tell what you will see before you open it?
curriculum.suits: a slow argument across a table

curriculum.title: Read the folios for tropes and textures
curriculum.make: Every held motif on the folios is found, sorted (texture, figure, saying) and linked to its pieces; one at a time, by hand, a candidate becomes a trope in the book or a texture under a plate.
curriculum.ask: Where did this idea come from, and how do we say so when we use it?
curriculum.suits: anyone who keeps a scrapbook; anyone who has had an idea taken without credit

curriculum.title: Letter the missing marks
curriculum.make: Digits, marks and the twelve sigils lettered on a ruled sheet like the first, scanned, traced; each penned glyph is replaced by a lettered one, and the set closes toward }.
curriculum.ask: What changes when the hand comes back to finish what the machine stood in for?
curriculum.suits: spwashi; anyone who wants to letter a sheet of their own

curriculum.title: A second hand
curriculum.make: Someone a generation away letters an alphabet on the same ruled sheet; the same tools trace it into a hand of its own, and the two are set side by side.
curriculum.ask: What does a hand say about who wrote it? What would you want a stranger to know about yours?
curriculum.suits: two people taking turns: one asks, one answers, then they swap

curriculum.title: Textures under the plates
curriculum.make: Folio textures (wash, scumble, drip, hatching) become grounds for the drawn studies and plates, each crediting its piece.
curriculum.ask: When a texture is borrowed into a new picture, does the picture owe the old one anything?
curriculum.suits: anyone who has made a collage

curriculum.title: Made on: texture, typography, physics
curriculum.make: Choose what the words are made on ($paper, $wash, $drip, $hatch, $honey, $glass, $storm): each brings a ground from a folio texture, a way of setting the hand, and physics — the letters become bodies you can drag, that sag or float or spring back.
curriculum.ask: Does a word mean something different when it moves like honey, or like a storm? Where else does the way something moves tell you how to feel about it?
curriculum.suits: restless hands that like to drag things; anyone who has noticed a sad song in a fast video

curriculum.title: Through spw.quest: read an address before you follow it
curriculum.make: Add a ? to an address and it passes through spw.quest: ?clarify says what it will show, ?align puts it in range, ?ground says it in another site's terms, ?mutate makes a variation — each with a receipt of what it did.
curriculum.ask: Read a link aloud before you open it: what do you expect? When something tidied or changed what you sent, did it tell you?
curriculum.suits: anyone who has been sent a link, and anyone reading one aloud to someone else
